tabs.title: People at the Beach
tabs.description: Understand the story and who helps.

tabs.title: Good Choices
tabs.description: Use the ideas to make a choice.

questions.q: Why are the cousins at the beach?
choices: They are working in a café.
They are on holiday and want to take photos.
They are looking for a lost dog.
They are studying for a maths test.
questions.explanation: The first paragraph says the cousins are on holiday and plan to take pictures.

questions.q: Why do the cousins take a bag that is not theirs?
choices: They want to sell the bag.
They think it belongs to Rosa.
They need another bag for sandwiches.
It is litter near the sea and they want to help.
questions.explanation: The cousins pick up plastic near the water even though it is not their own rubbish.

questions.q: What does Rosa think when she sees the cousins with the bag?
choices: She is pleased that they are helping.
She thinks they took something from her.
She asks them to leave at once.
She wants to stop the beach walk.
questions.explanation: Rosa smiles and thanks the cousins after seeing the bag.

questions.q: Why is rubbish on the beach also a problem for the sea?
choices: All rubbish turns into food for fish.
Plastic disappears when it is sunny.
The wind can blow it into the water.
The sea makes new cups every day.
questions.explanation: Rosa explains that evening wind can carry rubbish into the sea.

questions.q: How do the cousins feel after helping for an hour?
choices: They are angry because it is raining.
They are tired but happy with their work.
They are bored and want to go home.
They are afraid of the café owner.
questions.explanation: The fourth paragraph describes them as hot, tired and happy.

questions.q: What is a good thing about Eva's choice with her drink?
choices: She leaves the cup in the sand.
She throws the cup in the sea.
She gives the cup to a fish.
She keeps the cup for a rubbish bin.
questions.explanation: Eva buys a plastic cup but keeps it until she can put it in the bin.

questions.q: You bring your own bottle on a beach trip. Why can it help?
choices: You do not need a new plastic cup each time.
You can take home more sand.
You will never feel thirsty.
You can stop the wind.
questions.explanation: The narrator uses a personal bottle instead of a new disposable cup.

questions.q: Why might Rosa put Eva's photos on the café wall?
choices: The photos will make rubbish disappear.
The café needs more holiday posters.
The photos can help other people notice the problem.
Eva wants to sell the pictures.
questions.explanation: The final paragraph says people will be able to see the photos.

questions.q: What could you do if you see a bottle near a safe rubbish bin?
choices: Leave it beside the water.
Push it into the sea.
Wait for the wind to take it.
Put it in the bin if it is safe to pick up.
questions.explanation: The cousins collect litter carefully and use a nearby bin.

questions.q: What does the diary show about keeping a place clean?
choices: Only café owners can clean a beach.
Small good choices can help even when the beach is not perfect.
One hour makes all rubbish go away forever.
Only people who drop rubbish should pick it up.
questions.explanation: The fifth paragraph says the beach is not perfect, but the cousins leave their place clean.
